articles.title: Survival and Risk Factors of Implants Placed in Sites of Previous Failures-A Nationwide Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.summary: Across 177,410 implants, survival fell from 97.6% for first placements to 92.2% for second and 88.5% for third or later implants at the same site, with hazards of failure 4.6- and 5.7-fold higher respectively. Replacement implants in previously failed sites carry substantially greater risk and patients should be counselled accordingly.
articles.bottom_line: Quantify and disclose the markedly higher failure risk when re-implanting a failed site, and consider site modification or alternative prosthetics.

articles.title: Individualized healing significantly improves pink esthetics around immediate single implants: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: Meta-analysis of 20 studies (7 studies, 340 implants pooled) found anatomic healing abutments or immediate provisional restorations improved 1-year pink esthetic score by 2.54 points versus cylindrical healing abutments, with no difference in survival (>99%), marginal bone loss or patient satisfaction. Individualised healing components are a low-risk way to improve esthetic outcomes at immediate single implants.
articles.bottom_line: Use an anatomic healing abutment or immediate provisional rather than a stock cylindrical abutment on immediate single-tooth implants in the esthetic zone.

articles.title: Impact of Keratinized Mucosa Width and Mucosal Thickness on Implant Outcomes and Brushing Discomfort: A 25-Year Cohort Study.
articles.summary: In 149 patients followed a mean of 25 years, complete absence of keratinized mucosa was linked to greater crestal bone loss (0.28-0.40 mm more) and more soft-tissue dehiscence and platform visibility, while peri-implantitis prevalence (11.1% vs 0% vs 7.1%) and mucosal thickness showed no significant associations. In well-maintained patients, lack of keratinized mucosa is mainly an aesthetic/soft-tissue stability concern rather than a driver of peri-implant disease.
articles.bottom_line: Reserve keratinized tissue augmentation for sites with zero KMW where recession or platform exposure would matter aesthetically, rather than as blanket peri-implantitis prophylaxis.

articles.title: Clinical, Radiographic and Patient-Centred Outcomes of MINST Versus MIST With Enamel Matrix Derivative in Class II Mandibular Furcation Defects: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: In 40 patients with mandibular Class II furcation defects, flapless MINST plus EMD gave PPD reduction of 2.15 mm versus 2.20 mm for MIST plus EMD at 9 months, meeting non-inferiority with better patient-reported outcomes. A non-surgical, flapless EMD approach may achieve surgical-level results in these defects with less morbidity.
articles.bottom_line: Consider flapless MINST with EMD as a first-line, lower-morbidity alternative to MIST for Class II mandibular furcations.

articles.title: The Effect of Orthodontic Tooth Movement on Intrabony Periodontal Defects After Guided Tissue Regeneration. Part II: The Evaluation of Clinical and Radiological Parameters in a Randomised Controlled Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: In 34 patients, GTR of intrabony defects with orthodontic tooth movement started one week postoperatively achieved comparable CAL gain (4.0 vs 4.4 mm) and PPD reduction to GTR alone, and only the no-movement control group developed significant gingival recession and crestal bone loss. Early orthodontic movement after regenerative surgery does not compromise healing and may protect against recession.
articles.bottom_line: You can begin orthodontic movement about a week after GTR of intrabony defects without jeopardising regenerative outcomes.

articles.title: Autogenous bone grafting does not enhance bone repair in maxillary sinuses grafted with β-tricalcium phosphate: a split-mouth randomized controlled trial.
articles.summary: In 15 patients with bilateral sinus lifts, adding autogenous bone to β-TCP gave no advantage: 43.8% new bone versus 49.3% with β-TCP alone, and similar insertion torque and graft height at 10 months. Harvesting autogenous bone for sinus grafting with β-TCP adds morbidity without measurable benefit.
articles.bottom_line: Skip the autogenous bone harvest when grafting sinuses with β-TCP.

articles.title: Dentifrice formulations for the treatment of dentin hypersensitivity: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A network meta-analysis of 93 RCTs (9548 participants, 47 trials in the networks) found stannous fluoride and arginine-based dentifrices gave the most consistent and clinically meaningful reductions in dentin hypersensitivity at two weeks across tactile, evaporative and thermal stimuli. This gives a clear first-line product recommendation for a very common complaint.
articles.bottom_line: Recommend a stannous fluoride or arginine dentifrice as first-line self-applied therapy for dentin hypersensitivity.

articles.title: Prospective clinical study to evaluate the survival of two-piece zirconia implants: a single-center study. 36-month results.
articles.summary: In a prospective single-centre study, 9 of 23 two-piece zirconia CIM implants failed within 12 months, six from failed osseointegration, giving an alarmingly low survival at 36 months. This is a strong caution against routine use of this two-piece zirconia system in single-tooth sites.
articles.bottom_line: Avoid this two-piece zirconia implant system for routine single-tooth restorations pending better data.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of vestibular incision subperiosteal tunnel access (VISTA) technique with and without A-PRF impregnated with DFDBA in the treatment of recession defects in maxillary anterior region: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.summary: In a split-mouth RCT of 30 patients with multiple maxillary Miller Class I/II recessions, adding A-PRF impregnated with DFDBA to VISTA gave significantly greater CAL gain and recession reduction at 12 months than VISTA alone. The combined biologic-graft adjunct may improve root coverage outcomes and labial plate thickness in multiple recession cases.
articles.bottom_line: Consider adding A-PRF plus DFDBA when treating multiple maxillary recessions with VISTA.

articles.title: Segmental Intentional Replantation for the Management of Large Periapical Cystic Lesions: Technical Report and a Case Series.
articles.summary: Eight teeth in seven patients treated with segmental intentional replantation for large periapical cysts were all retained with probing depths ≤3 mm, mean extraoral time under 17 minutes, and marginal bone change of only 0.02 mm. The technique offers an alternative to extraction or extensive apicoectomy for large cystic lesions in skilled hands.
articles.bottom_line: A reproducible new option worth learning for large periapical cysts, pending larger series.

articles.title: Tunnel Technique With Connective Tissue Graft Versus Free Gingival Graft for Multiple Gingival Recessions in the Anterior Mandible: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: In a 12-month RCT of multiple mandibular anterior recessions, both tunnel-plus-connective-tissue-graft and free gingival graft significantly reduced recession depth, with FGG giving more predictable keratinized tissue gain and the tunnel technique giving better healing outcomes. Clinicians can choose based on whether keratinized tissue width or patient comfort/aesthetics is the priority.
articles.bottom_line: Use FGG when keratinized tissue gain is the goal and tunnel+CTG when healing and aesthetics matter more in the anterior mandible.

articles.title: The Causal Effect of Supra- and Sub-Gingival Instrumentation on the Oral Microbiome of Elderly Periodontitis Patients Treated in Nursing Homes: Secondary Analysis of a Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: In 36 nursing home residents (mean age 85) randomised to a mean 14-minute session of supra- and subgingival instrumentation or control, the treated group showed reduced dysbiosis (β = -1.97, p = 0.0008) plus BOP falling from 45% to 35% and mean PPD from 4.5 to 4.0 mm at 3 months. Brief, pragmatic outreach instrumentation delivers measurable clinical and microbial benefit in frail elderly patients.
articles.bottom_line: Short outreach debridement visits are worth offering to institutionalised elderly patients rather than deferring care.
